_wilmslowPiccolinoCiboSource: Piccolino Grande and Cibo Gran Cafe added 2026-09-18 at explicit user request (named directly: 'piccolino's gran cafe, cibo gran cafe' — the user knows both personally). Both are exactly the case the two-gate model (CLAUDE.md Hard rule 1, 2026-09-16) was built for: real multi-site groups that the old single chain-veto would have excluded outright, now judged on Gate 1/Gate 2 instead. Piccolino Grande, 6-12 Swan Street (postcode SK9 1HE, geocoded via postcodes.io) is part of the national Piccolino chain (Individual Restaurants) — verified via piccolinorestaurants.com, confidentials.com and themanc.com as a GBP 2m, 2026 rebuild described as Piccolino's most ambitious site outside London (marble/brass/terrazzo interior, copper-clad pizza oven, a winterised Tuscan terrace, a tableside 'carbonara grande' and Fassona Piedmontese T-bone). Gate 1: passes cleanly — an upscale, well-regarded premium-casual group, not mass-market high-street. Gate 2 distinctiveness: 3 — CLAUDE.md's own worked example ('a good Piccolino') is this exact case; the flagship-tier rebuild argues for the top of that band rather than a generic 3, but the format is still a familiar national brand, not singular. ownership='group'. Cibo Gran Cafe, 31-33 Grove Arcade (postcode SK9 1DU) is the newer sibling site to the already-seeded Cibo (26-28 Green Lane, two minutes away) — verified via ciborestaurants.co.uk and squaremeal.co.uk as a combined bar/ristorante/artisanal-patisserie format with private event space (90 seated/150 standing) and a Sunday afternoon tea. Researching this site surfaced that Cibo Restaurants is a real 5-site regional group (Manchester, Hale, two Wilmslow sites, Disley), not the single independent restaurant the existing Cibo entry's ownership defaulted to under migration 0009's blanket backfill (distinctiveness=4/ownership='independent' applied to all 244 pre-existing rows) — that default is corrected alongside this addition (ownership -> 'small_group') rather than left silently wrong now that real research contradicts it. Cibo Gran Cafe Gate 1: passes (same small regional group, same quality bar). Gate 2 distinctiveness: 3 — a genuinely less common combined format for the area, but still a recognisable extension of an existing local brand rather than a singular find. ownership='small_group'. Both venues' dietary tags (vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free) are sourced, not assumed: Piccolino's own allergen pages confirm gluten-free pasta and vegan substitutions on request; Cibo Gran Cafe's listings confirm vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free options (though guest feedback on gluten-free handling there is mixed — flagged, not hidden). BRUNCH SPOT (already used for Caramello) reused for Cibo Gran Cafe rather than inventing a new type, since its daytime cafe/patisserie identity fits that tile cleanly. Distinctiveness/ownership values here are documented in this note and applied directly via SQL (supabase/migrations/0013_wilmslow_piccolino_cibo.sql) — not stored as JSON fields on the venue entries below, since no other entry in this file carries those fields yet and adding them to only two would make the schema inconsistent; the live database is the real source of truth for those two columns going forward (see 0010_growth_engine.sql's own source-of-truth-flip note). One more thing surfaced re-reading _wilmslowDensitySource below: its chain-exclusion list from the original August pass (Slug & Lettuce, Revolution, The Botanist, Unico Lounge/The Lounges, Anthology/Greene King, The King William/Robinsons, Stanneylands/JW Lees) is the same kind of list that produced the Mouro Coffee Bar re-evaluation candidate elsewhere — worth a fresh Gate 1/Gate 2 pass, not done as part of this addition.

Flagged for whoever runs this job next: retry the full queue once WebSearch/WebFetch are confirmed working again — today's small promotion (3 of 14 actionable items) reflects a tooling outage, not a thin queue.

This prompted two changes to the daily research/review agent briefs (.claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md, .claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md): checking a candidate is real and non-chain was never the same as checking it's still open today, and neither brief previously re-verified already-promoted venues at all — see those files' own updated 'still operating' guidance. Coordinates: Greece has no UK-style postcode API, so geocoding used Nominatim (OpenStreetMap's free geocoder, 1 req/sec rate-limited per its usage policy) with each venue's real found address as the query; roughly half resolved to a precise point, the rest fell back to their real village/beach-area centroid (e.g. Perivolos beach's own OSM polygon centroid) with small manual spread within that area's real bounding box so venues on the same beach or caldera strip don't stack on one exact pixel — an honest area-level approximation, not a fabricated precise address, matching this file's own established 'skip rather than guess' standard applied to location precision instead of venue identity.
